Several people have asked my why I no longer post about and discuss China's monthly economic data releases. The answer is because there are only a limited number of ways I can make the same set of comments:

a) industrial production grew, but less than expected,

b) retail sales grew by even less, thus worsening the domestic imbalances further,

c) it is increasingly hard to find investment opportunities, even as Beijing cannot allow investment growth to decelerate,

d) in order to prevent GDP growth from slowing to politically unacceptable levels, debt continues to grow at the fastest pace of any country in history, and

e) the trade surplus was unexpectedly large this month.
https://t.co/zqCLrbnbZR

As Setser notes, a revaluation of the RMB is a necessary part of any reasonable global rebalancing. It is not the only policy, nor even necessarily the best policy, but it is the only realistic policy that can be implemented quickly enough to matter to China's trade partners, even if -- for that very reason -- this also makes it hard for Beijing, who would prefer a much slower rebalancing.

Caixin: "China’s top financial regulator reported the elimination of 670 rural small and midsize banks as authorities pressed ahead with a broad sector overhaul. The consolidation underscores Beijing’s escalating effort to contain risks in the country’s fragile regional banking system through mergers and acquisitions, creating larger and better-capitalized institutions to help withstand economic pressure. Even so, asset quality remains a key challenge. A recent report from the Shanghai Institution for Finance and Development said regional banks continue to face pressure from local government financing vehicles, retail lending and the property sector, particularly in lower-tier cities."
https://t.co/TGI7ZhV4N0

Xinhua: "China unveiled a set of measures to further stimulate consumption in lower-tier markets. It calls for upgrading consumption channels in counties, including renovating township commercial centers, rural markets and local fairs, attracting domestic and international brands to open regional debut stores, and encouraging the redevelopment of existing land resources."

The authorities, in other words, will do everything they can to boost the role of consumption as a driver of growth as long as that only means spending to further support the supply side of the consumption economy.  

What they still won't do is spend money to support the demand side – i.e. shift income to households – even though by now it should be obvious that when it comes to boosting consumption, the only constraint is on the demand side.

Alibaba T-Head's Xuantie RISC-V team announces Day 0 support for Qwen-3.8 model, especially the 27B one.

Its 64-core C950 CPU (w/ RVV support) can decode at 30 tps w/ 1.9s TTFT.

Xuantie family has wide series of RISC-V chips for different edge applications. Ali can now sell the chips needed for its own chips. It can also install them in its Data Centers for inference of smaller models.

They've also paired C950 to work w/ specialised AI accelerators like 江原科技 D20 & Rockchip RK1828.

Will RISC-V solution from T-Head get really into AIPC mkt?
